name: Drevka Tamarind-Anise Hard Drops
description: Small, oval hard drops with a deep burgundy-brown color, combining tart tamarind with the slow, medicinal warmth of star anise. A throwback format — no smart packaging, no mood compounds, just synth-sugar and flavor. Sold in small paper twist bags.
flavor_profile: Sharp tamarind sourness that opens into a warm, licorice-adjacent anise depth — long finish, slightly astringent
price: Φ1.10 for a twist bag of 8
cultural_context: Popular among older Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents who grew up with similar regional hard candies before standardization flattened the market. Younger buyers sometimes pick them up ironically, then come back for real. The paper twist bag is considered charmingly anachronistic.
story_hooks: The Drevka family recipe was allegedly lifted from a pre-Corponation era confectioner — a descendant shows up at the M88 small claims tribunal with documentation.
A Tier 1 fixer uses Drevka twist bags as a dead-drop marker — a bag left on a specific bench means the meeting is safe to proceed.

A food historian doing a mesh documentary on pre-collapse regional candy traditions tracks down the Drevka factory and finds it's one of only three places still using a specific flavor-extraction technique that's nearly extinct.
